thesis_edits: Replace '20,000+ service providers' with '~19,000 utility-system contractors (Census 2017: 18,877 firms, 570,952 employees), mostly small; ~240 DCA gas distribution members; platform-quality maintenance firms in the low hundreds (est.)'.

Replace '<10 meaningful scaled players' with '15-20 players with revenue around or above $1B (Quanta, MasTec, Primoris, Asplundh, MYR, Centuri, Artera, Azuria/Inframark, Davey, Pike, Day & Zimmermann, Michels) plus 26 sponsor-backed platforms; fewer than 10 per sub-segment; none spans gas, power and water at scale'.

Replace '70% of the US electric grid is over 25 years old' with 'DOE: >70% of transmission lines and power transformers are 25+ years old; NREL: 50-55% of 60-80M distribution transformers are older than 33 years, and only 2.5-3% are replaced or added each year'.

Restate the gas statistic as 'PHMSA: 28% of distribution pipe was installed before 1970; ~16,300 miles of cast and wrought iron remain (2023); bare-steel programs run to ~2041'. Re-pull the CY2024 by-decade inventory before publishing.

Quantify water: '11.1 breaks per 100 miles a year, ~260,000 breaks and $2.6B of repairs annually, $452B of pipe past useful life (Utah State 2023); mains replaced on a ~125-year cycle'. Label $625B as a 20-year need, not funded spend.

Slide 6: delete 'crews flex across segments' and 'specialized assets move across jobs and regions' as applied between gas/water and power. Replace with 'gas and water share underground crews and fleet (~53% / ~65%, est.); holdco synergies are density, purchasing, insurance, safety and back office'.
Add a TAM slide: ~$44-81B a year of outsourced MRO (gas $12-20B, T&D $20-35B, power-gen $4-8B, water $8-18B; all estimates).

Add an economics slide: comparables earn 8-10% adj. EBITDA on MSA work and 12-24% in specialty niches; the illustrative platform earns 9-11% with no margin expansion; returns come from cash yield at ~6-8x entry, not multiple arbitrage.

Rewrite the why-now around replacement capex that utilities recover through their rates (EEI ~$208B in 2025; AGA $49.1B in 2023), mandated gas compliance cycles, and asset life extension (nuclear to 80 years, poles to 70-80+). Drop population, and note that load growth mostly funds construction.
Add a precedents slide: winners (Shermco, Pike, USIC, Osmose, Badger), failures (Artera, Williams, Orbital, Team), and the lessons (focus, low leverage, no fixed-price creep).

Change the sequencing from 'first unit natural gas or power' to 'gas first; water as an adjacency in the same metros; T&D as a separate, later company; power-gen only via testing and inspection add-ons'.

Tighten the platform criteria: at least two utility MSAs; most revenue from MSA or unit-rate maintenance; a clean OSHA and EMR record; a documented operator-qualification program; an owned fleet; and explicit leverage limits.

synthesis.caveats:
This synthesis ran no new web searches. It relies on the research, verification and candidate passes.

Many central figures are analyst estimates, not reported data:
- the TAM by unit ($44-81B)
- the labor and fleet overlap matrices
- synergy basis points
- the illustrative P&L and margin bridge
- the size of the platform-quality universe
- the pre-tax cash yield

Items that are unverified or weakly sourced:
- The 1921 build date of PG&E's Caribou-Palermo line.
- MIT's 8,000 mi/yr transmission build rate (excluded) and the ~90% replacement share of transmission spend.
- Artera's current rating (a Dec 2025 S&P action was not confirmed).
- Pike's >$5B value (press-reported).
- Asplundh's revenue and Day & Zimmermann's current revenue.
- The current owners of USG Water Solutions, Heath Consultants, Pittsburg Tank & Tower and Maguire Iron, and J.W. Didado's ownership.
- The PJM +41% wholesale price figure.

Six-digit NAICS firm counts conflict across aggregators and were not used. The gas 'mains over 50 years' statistic rests on 2021 PHMSA data and should be re-pulled.

The candidate list over-represents sponsor-owned and web-visible firms. Founder-owned $10-50M businesses need primary rosters (DCA, NETA, NASSCO, AWWA, state PUC lists). Lower-middle-market multiples are all-industry (GF Data), not utility-specific.

Not researched here: state gas-transition policy and long-run gas demand.

Out of scope: sponsor compensation and any specific live deal process.
